dt-example.title: API - User defined states
dt-example.info:
So far, the bookmark examples for StateRestore have focused on predefined states. However, it is of course possible to allow bookmarks to states that the end user creates. It requires a small amount of code to create the links, since they need to update automatically whenever the states list changes.
We know when the states list is changed through the `-event stateRestore` event, and `api stateRestore.states().details()` can be used to get the list of states available. From there it is just a bit of DOM building! In this example I've used `-type DataTable.Dom` as a DOM library to create the elements, but you can use `document.createElement` or any other library you prefer.
To use this example, create a few tables states (changing the ordering, page length, search to create unique states) and you'll see that for each a new link appears in the output box. Click on the link to have the state load.
